audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Akshan Level 1 outright and never handed 2+ items to Ryze — it ended on three consecutive 'Skill' rows while Ryze wins 52.11% and the page's own late block says a stacked Seraph's beats him outright.
audit.why: Overload (Q) is 1000 range against Avengerang's 850, so level 1 is not Akshan's — it is contested at worst. At two items the page already argues Ryze wins; the enum never said so.
audit.corrected: Level 1 to Skill and 2+ items to Ryze in both layers as matched pairs, ratings moved to 5/10 and 7/10. Levels 4-5 and First item left as Skill rather than flipped to the packet's Akshan, because the mirror (akshan__ryze) was audited without touching those rows and I will not introduce a disagreement it did not make.

audit.why: Four spikes present with sensible timings (Lvl 1, Lvl 3-5, 1st item, 2+ items), and the mirror confirms the count was left intact there too.
audit.corrected: No count change; spikes[0].text corrected for the range error noted under point 4.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0].text and the early block both say Ryze must 'reach melee range' or 'enter melee range' to use Spell Flux. whys[2] calls the combo an 'E-Q-W chain'. Dirty Fighting's shield is never mentioned anywhere on the page.
audit.why: Spell Flux (E) is 615 range and Rune Prison (W) is 615 — neither is melee, and Overload is 1000. The root order is E-Flux first, then W to convert the slow into a root, then Q; the mirror flags 'E-Q root' as a systemic template error. Dirty Fighting shields Akshan on every third hit from his attacks and abilities against a champion, which eats exactly the burst window Ryze opens with.
audit.corrected: Real ranges given (1000 Q, 615 E/W against his 850 Q), the chain restated in the correct order, and the third-hit shield added as the thing to bait out before committing.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d was placeholder text asserting Akshan 'spends Heroic Swing early' as a guarantee, with no number.
audit.why: Heroic Swing is 18s at rank 1, dropping to 12s at rank 5 — that downtime is the actual window in which Rune Prison lands.
audit.corrected: The 18s rank-1 gap stated as the root window.

edits.before: Only Q available and Akshan's Avengerang arc pokes you from outside Spell Flux bounce range — walk behind minions and last-hit at safe distance.
edits.after: Overload (Q) reaches 1000 against Avengerang's 850, but his arc still outranges Spell Flux's 615 — poke on Q's 5s cooldown and last-hit from behind minions.

edits.before: His full kit is online including Heroic Swing — he dodges your W root mid-combo and resets spacing, breaking the E-Q-W chain you need for real damage.
edits.after: His full kit is online including Heroic Swing — he swings off your root mid-combo and resets spacing, breaking the E-Flux into W-root into Q chain you need.

edits.before: Akshan's Q (Avengerang) arc poke hits you before you can reach melee range for Spell Flux — stand behind minions and only move up to last-hit with your own Q.
edits.after: Avengerang arcs 850 and Spell Flux only reaches 615, so he pokes you the whole way in — stand behind minions and answer with Overload, which outranges him at 1000.

edits.before: At level 1 you have Q only and must enter melee range to Flux-stack — Akshan punishes exactly that with Avengerang arc pokes that hit both sides of the boomerang path. Stand at max Q range behind the wave, last-hit safely, and skip any trade where he has his Q up. At level 2 your W root is online but Akshan's Heroic Swing is not yet — this is a brief window where a clean W-into-empowered-Q can land, so threaten the root if he pushes up. By level 3 his E grapple arrives and the spacing war begins in earnest: Akshan will swing away from your W every time you try to pin him, so only commit to the root when you have vision of where he can grapple to and a minion or wall blocks the escape angle.
edits.after: At level 1 you have Overload only — 1000 range, so you actually outrange his 850 Avengerang, but Spell Flux needs 615 and that walk in is what his boomerang punishes on both legs of its path. Poke on Q's flat 5s cooldown from behind the wave and skip any trade where his Q is up. At level 2 your W root is online and Heroic Swing is not — a brief window where a clean Flux-into-root-into-Q can land, so threaten it if he pushes up. By level 3 his grapple arrives and the spacing war starts: he needs terrain to anchor the swing, so only commit the root when you can see the wall he would swing to and a minion or the wave blocks that angle.

edits.before: Akshan spends Heroic Swing early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Heroic Swing is down 18s at rank 1 — that gap is when your root actually lands.

edits.before: That’s Akshan’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Every third Dirty Fighting hit shields him — bait that shield before you burst.

notes: The packet suspectName 'Use Heroic Swing' is a false positive — Heroic Swing is the correct E name. Confirming the mirror's systemic finding from this side: the template's 'E-Q root chain' phrasing is wrong wherever it appears; Ryze's root is Spell Flux (E) then Rune Prison (W), and Overload's bonus against a Fluxed target is extra damage from his R passive, not crowd control. whys[2] carried it here. Levels 4-5 and First item are 'Skill' in both layers here but 'Akshan' in the packet chart — I left them alone deliberately rather than flip rows the mirror audit did not touch; worth a deliberate decision at champion level.
